addedLines: - agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-py: Use this agent to verify that a Python Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a Python Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)

- agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-ts: Use this agent to verify that a TypeScript Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a TypeScript Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- feature-dev:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- plugin-dev:agent-creator: Use this agent when the user asks to "create an agent", "generate an agent", "build a new agent", "make me an agent that...", or describes agent functionality they need. Trigger when user wants to create autonomous agents for plugins. Examples:

<example>
Context: User wants to create a code review agent
user: "Create an agent that reviews code for quality issues"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate the agent configuration."
<commentary>
User requesting new agent creation, trigger agent-creator to generate it.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>

</example>

<example>

assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate a configuration validator agent."
<commentary>
Plugin development with agent addition, trigger agent-creator.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Write, Read)

<example>

- plugin-dev:skill-reviewer: Use this agent when the user has created or modified a skill and needs quality review, asks to "review my skill", "check skill quality", "improve skill description", or wants to ensure skill follows best practices. Trigger proactively after skill creation. Examples:

</example>

Skill description modified, review for triggering effectiveness.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_f… [truncated]

- playwright-skill: Complete browser automation with Playwright. Auto-detects dev servers, writes clean test scripts to /tmp. Test pages, fill forms, take screenshots, check responsive design, validate UX, test login flows, check links, automate any browser task. Use when user wants to test websites, automate browser interactions, validate web functionality, or perform any browser-based testing.
- audit-tier: Identify the protection tier, owner, and import blast radius of a file or directory under overrides/. Use before editing anything you're unsure about.
- code-quality: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
- code-review: AI-powered code review using CodeRabbit. Default code-review skill. Trigger for any explicit review request AND autonomously when the agent thinks a review is needed (code/PR/quality/security).
- contentful-register-component: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component.
- feature-spec: Turn a plain-English feature request into a scoped implementation plan before any code is written. Asks one clarifying question at a time, then produces a spec Claude Code can execute safely. Use this before starting any non-trivial implementation session.
- generate-changelog: Generate a release changelog from conventional commits and upstream baseline notes. Produces audience-specific outputs for the dev team, QA, product, and GitHub Release. Use before cutting a release branch or when preparing release notes.
- new-component: Scaffold a new Zimmermann component under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript, Chakra-first, with a paired Storybook story. Use whenever a new custom component is needed.
- onboarding: Interactive onboarding for new developers and QA engineers joining the Zimmermann PWA Kit project. Asks role at the start, checks the mechanical setup items, then orients the person to the rules and tools relevant to their role and squad. Run this in the first Claude Code session on a new machine or a first day on the project.
- pr-checklist: Generate a PR description and merge checklist based on the files changed on the current branch. Pairs with /code-quality.
- project-init: One-time project setup walkthrough. Runs the state detection script, fixes automatable items, asks one question at a time for human-input items, and updates the 7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist Confluence page as each item is confirmed. Run this once when setting up the project for the first time, or when returning to check setup status.
- qa-generate: Generate a Gherkin .feature file and Playwright test spec from a Jira story. Human-in-the-lead — Lead QA validates the .feature before Playwright is generated. Use for any new storefront user journey that needs E2E test coverage.
- scope-check: Review a proposed Claude Code prompt for scope safety before it runs. Classifies every likely-touched file by tier and verdicts the prompt SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED, rewriting it when needed.
- session-start: Run the mandatory session start ritual — reads tracking docs, runs branch + health checks, states current position. Use at the start of every coding session.
- upstream-sync-review: Review the release notes / changelog for a new @salesforce/retail-react-app version before bumping. Lightweight policy — see .docs/upstreamPolicy.md.
- code-review:code-review: Code review a pull request
- feature-dev:feature-dev: Guided feature development with codebase understanding and architecture focus
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- commit-commands:clean_gone: Cleans up all git branches marked as [gone] (branches that have been deleted on the remote but still exist locally), including removing associated worktrees.
- commit-commands:commit-push-pr: Commit, push, and open a PR
- commit-commands:commit: Create a git commit
- claude-md-management:revise-claude-md: Update CLAUDE.md with learnings from this session
- pr-review-toolkit:review-pr: Comprehensive PR review using specialized agents
- agent-sdk-dev:new-sdk-app: Create and setup a new Claude Agent SDK application
- plugin-dev:create-plugin: Guided end-to-end plugin creation workflow with component design, implementation, and validation
- vercel:bootstrap: Bootstrap a repository with Vercel-linked resources by running preflight checks, provisioning integrations, verifying env keys, and then executing db/dev startup commands safely.
- vercel:deploy: Deploy the current project to Vercel. Pass "prod" or "production" as argument to deploy to production. Default is preview deployment.
- vercel:env: Manage Vercel environment variables. Commands include list, pull, add, remove, and diff. Use to sync environment variables between Vercel and your local development environment.
- vercel:status: Show the status of the current Vercel project — recent deployments, linked project info, and environment overview.
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- superpowers:brainstorming: You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior. Explores user intent, requirements and design before implementation.
- superpowers:dispatching-parallel-agents: Use when facing 2+ independent tasks that can be worked on without shared state or sequential dependencies
- superpowers:executing-plans: Use when you have a written implementation plan to execute in a separate session with review checkpoints
- superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch: Use when implementation is complete, all tests pass, and you need to decide how to integrate the work
- superpowers:receiving-code-review: Use when receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions, especially if feedback seems unclear or technically questionable - requires technical rigor and verification, not performative agreement or blind implementation
- superpowers:requesting-code-review: Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements
- superpowers:subagent-driven-development: Use when executing implementation plans with independent tasks in the current session
- superpowers:systematic-debugging: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes
- superpowers:test-driven-development: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code
- superpowers:using-git-worktrees: Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from current workspace or before executing implementation plans - ensures an isolated workspace exists via native tools or git worktree fallback
- superpowers:using-superpowers: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring skill invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions
- superpowers:verification-before-completion: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always
- superpowers:writing-plans: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code
- superpowers:writing-skills: Use when creating new skills, editing existing skills, or verifying skills work before deployment
- claude-md-management:claude-md-improver: Audit and improve CLAUDE.md files in repositories. Use when user asks to check, audit, update, improve, or fix CLAUDE.md files. Scans for all CLAUDE.md files, evaluates quality against templates, outputs quality report, then makes targeted updates. Also use when the user mentions "CLAUDE.md maintenance" or "project memory optimization".
- figma:figma-code-connect: Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.
- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.
- figma:figma-swiftui: SwiftUI ↔ Figma translation. Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Routes to a direction-specific reference doc; loads alongside `figma-use` for the code → design path.
- figma:figma-use: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `use_figma` tool call. NEVER call `use_figma` directly without loading this skill first. Skipping it causes common, hard-to-debug failures. Trigger whenever the user wants to perform a write action or a unique read action that requires JavaScript execution in the Figma file context — e.g. create/edit/delete nodes, set up variables or tokens, build components and variants, modify auto-layout or fills, bind variables to properties, or inspect file structure programmatically.
- figma:figma-use-figjam: This skill helps agents use Figma's use_figma MCP tool in the FigJam context. Can be used alongside figma-use which has foundational context for using the use_figma tool.
- figma:figma-use-motion: Motion / animation context for the `use_figma` MCP tool — animating Figma nodes via manual keyframes, animation styles, easing, and timeline duration. Load alongside figma-use whenever a task involves adding, editing, or inspecting animation on a node.
- figma:figma-use-slides: This skill helps agents use Figma's use_figma MCP tool in the Slides context. Can be used alongside figma-use which has foundational context for using the use_figma tool.
- claude-code-setup:claude-automation-recommender: Analyze a codebase and recommend Claude Code automations (hooks, subagents, skills, plugins, MCP servers). Here's the full picture on **PR #43**, pitched for you as FE lead.

## TL;DR
A Contentful "live preview" feature so content editors can see draft content in the real storefront before publishing. The **code** is in good shape — every substantive CodeRabbit finding is fixed — but it's **not mergeable yet**: no human approval, the branch is behind `develop`, one CI job is red, and two documentation threads are still open (including the PR's own description being out of date).

---

## The basics

| | |
|---|---|
| **Title** | `feat(contentful): add Contentful Studio live preview and Experience pages` |
| **Author** | `mani060689` (not you) |
| **Branch** | `feature/storefront-preview-contentful` → `develop` |
| **Jira** | [SFCC-49](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-49) |
| **Size** | +368 / −89 across 11 files |
| **Age** | Opened 28 Jul, last updated 29 Jul · **OPEN**, not draft |
| **Review decision** | ⚠️ **CHANGES_REQUESTED** · **Mergeable but BEHIND** `develop` |

## What it actually does (ELI5)

Contentful is the CMS. Editors want to preview *unpublished* content on the live site. This PR wires that up **two ways**:

1. **A new `/preview` page** (`ContentfulPreview`) — a dedicated route that talks to Contentful's *Preview* API and gets real-time updates as an editor types (via the Live Preview SDK's `postMessage` channel).
2. **A `?preview` switch on existing Experience pages** — add `?preview` to a normal page URL to flip that same page into draft-preview mode.

Plus three supporting bits:
- **`<Seo noIndex />`** on both preview paths, so Google never indexes draft content.
- **Extracted an `ExperienceFetch` child component** to fix a React **Rules-of-Hooks violation** (a data-fetch hook was being called conditionally after an early return — classic bug).
- **New shared constants** in `config/contentful.ts` (hostnames, fallback locale).

## The one design decision you'll care about 🔑

**The Contentful Preview (CPA) token runs client-side.** It has to — the Live Preview SDK needs it in the browser for real-time `postMessage` updates. That's a token in the client bundle, which normally raises an eyebrow. Their mitigation, three layers:

1. Token is **only** set in Managed Runtime on **dev/test/sit/uat — never staging/prod**.
2. Both preview routes **return 404 when the token is absent** (so they're inert in prod).
3. Both are **`noindex`**.

This is a deliberate, documented tradeoff — worth your explicit sign-off since it's the kind of thing a security review will ask about. Note `config/contentful.ts` is **Tier 1**, but the change is **additive-only** (new constants, no existing logic touched), so CODEOWNERS will auto-request `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`.

## Files & tiers

| File | Tier | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `pages/contentfulPreview/index.tsx` (+208) | 4 | New page |
| `pages/experience/index.tsx` (+119/−68) | 4 | `?preview` support + hooks fix |
| `config/contentful.ts` (+5) | **1** | Additive constants → tier-1 review |
| `routes.tsx` (+8/−1) | **2** | Registers `/preview` → **needs non-author + cross-squad review** |
| `types/vendor.d.ts` (+5/−3) | — | Made `res.status()` chainable |
| `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` (+10/−6) | 4 | Doc updates |
| `.claude/registry/*.md` ×5 | — | Auto-generated metadata |

## CI status — 9 green, 1 red

✅ Vitest · Storybook a11y · Playwright (localhost) · CodeRabbit · Branch Target · **Tier 1 Frozen Files** · Cross-Squad Boundary · Tier 2 Protected Files
❌ **Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)** — but the failure is `Error: Config file does not exist...` — a **BrowserStack tooling/config problem, not a test failing on their code**. This PR doesn't touch `.browserstack.yml`, so it's almost certainly a CI-environment issue (would hit any PR), needing a rerun or a CI fix rather than a code change here.

## Review status — code fixed, docs lagging

CodeRabbit is currently the **only** reviewer (a bot), sitting at Changes Requested. The good news: **all the real code findings are resolved:**

- 🔴 **Rules-of-Hooks violation** (`experience:116`) — ✅ fixed (the `ExperienceFetch` extraction)
- 🟠 **404 not-found not properly signalled** (`contentfulPreview:180`) — ✅ fixed
- 🟠 **Silent preview→delivery fallback vs. the fail-explicitly rule** (`experience:93`) — ✅ fixed

**Two threads remain open — both documentation/metadata, not code:**

- 🟠 **`02-contentful.md:60`** — the doc still describes the *old silent delivery-mode fallback*, which the code no longer does. **And the PR's own Summary still describes that old behaviour too.** So the description you're reading is itself slightly stale — worth knowing before you evaluate it.
- 🟡 **`.claude/registry/pages.md`** — generated registry lists `EnvSelector`/`ProductList` pages that don't exist on this branch (stale rows).

Per the repo rule, every CodeRabbit finding needs an in-thread reply (fixed *or* justified) before merge — those two still need closing out.

## What's blocking merge

1. **No human approval yet** — needs a non-author developer (for `routes.tsx`, Tier 2 + cross-squad) **and** a `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` code-owner review (for `config/contentful.ts`, Tier 1, enforced by branch protection).
2. **Branch is BEHIND `develop`** (~14 commits — all the env-sync/CI work from PRs #42/#44/#45, none Contentful-related, so a clean-ish update).
3. **BrowserStack red** must go green or be formally waived as infra.
4. **Two open review threads** to resolve/reply.

## One latent hazard I checked for you

There's an unmerged branch (`feature/agent-docs-cleanup`) that relocates `.docs/` → `.claude/docs/`. **I confirmed it hasn't landed on `develop` yet**, so this PR's edit to `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` is fine *right now*. But if that cleanup merges first, this PR will conflict on that file — a sequencing thing to keep on your radar.

---

**My read:** solid feature, the hard engineering (hooks fix, 404 gating, noindex) is done and reviewed. It's stuck on process, not code — get the branch updated, sort the BrowserStack infra failure, tidy the two doc threads (and refresh the now-stale PR summary), then route it for the Tier 1 + non-author human reviews. why is this list different from the last comment i posted on this PR as i requested for changes? Review: Requesting Changes
I'm requesting changes on one item before merge, plus a couple of should-fixes. The must-fix is verified against the live branch and is really yours to call, since you own both the code and the integration doc it touches.

Must Resolve Before Merge
1. The ?preview no-token path is a three-way mismatch between the two preview routes and the doc.
CodeRabbit flagged that .docs/integration/02-contentful.md still says ?preview Experience pages "fall back to Delivery API mode" with no token, and it's right that the code no longer does that. But the more important half is what the code does do now, which CodeRabbit didn't reach: in experience/index.tsx (L100–108), previewUnavailable short-circuits to an explicit "Preview is not enabled in this environment" message rendered at HTTP 200 with no <Seo noIndex/>. Its sibling /preview route handles the same no-token condition properly — res.status(404) + noindex (contentfulPreview/index.tsx L168–179). So the two preview entry points disagree, and on prod (where the CPA token is deliberately absent) /<real-slug>?preview becomes an indexable 200 — the missing half of the noindex gate from my #41 review. The doc compounds it: §9 (L128) even asserts "Both preview paths are noindex," which the code currently contradicts.

Fix: bring the previewUnavailable branch in line with /preview — add <Seo noIndex/> and a 404 via useServerContext() (the file already imports Seo; it doesn't yet import useServerContext, so that's the one addition) — then update the three doc references (the §3 diagram comment, the §4 CPA row, and the §9 bullet at L128) to describe the real behaviour: both paths fail explicitly, both noindex, no delivery fallback.

Should-Fix
Both pages duplicate the getContentfulConfig() → useMemo(createClient) block. Extract a single useContentfulClient hook — it's also the natural home for the token/host logic. (CodeRabbit has flagged this repeatedly.)
The new files don't pass npm run lint — ~100 Prettier errors (semicolons / brace-spacing). Run npm run lint:fix before merge.
(Optional) contentfulPreview/index.tsx L117 keeps locale in the getEntry effect's deps, but the effect only resolves the entry's content type, which is locale-independent — so a locale change triggers a redundant refetch + spinner flash on the /preview route. Harmless (the active guard covers the race) and editor-only; worth the one-token trim only since you're already in the file. Your call.

- Promotions engine and multi-currency/FX pricebook setup
- CI workflow split — two complementary workflows, each with a clear role:
  - `qa.yml` (every PR to `develop`/`release/**`): `unit-tests` (Vitest) + `storybook-test` (Storybook `play` + `@storybook/addon-a11y`, `storybook test --ci`) run in parallel; `e2e-browserstack` on release PRs only. **`storybook-test` job is wired but pending `@storybook/addon-test` and `@storybook/addon-a11y` installation (feature/storybook-v10 upgrade task).**
  - `digital-sit.yml` (push/PR to `release/**`): four parallel jobs into `sit-gate` — `playwright-p0` (Chromium P0 suite), `bundle-size` (bundlewatch, main.js < 180 kB / vendor.js < 250 kB / main.css < 50 kB), `contract-tests` (placeholder; real MuleSoft OpenAPI assertion pending spec source), `lighthouse-ci` (Perf ≥ 80, A11y ≥ 90, Best Practices ≥ 90; requires LHCI server secrets)
- **`e2e-localhost` (qa.yml) is fixed and re-enabled, as of PR #35 (`bugfix/ci-e2e-test`, merged 2026-07-16).** Root cause of the "homepage smoke test fails in CI, logo never found" issue (open as of PR #30): `BasePage.js`'s old `dismissConsent()` wrapped both `waitFor()` and `.click()` in one `try/catch`, so a real click failure was silently swallowed as "no dialog appeared" — if a consent dialog genuinely appeared in CI (injected by something outside this repo's own source, e.g. GTM/MRT platform config — not by anything grep-visible in `overrides/`) and the click failed transiently, the `aria-modal` dialog stayed open and blocked the entire page's accessibility tree, exactly matching the symptom. Fixed by CodeRabbit-prompted review in PR #30 (separated `.click()` out of the `try/catch`) — but that fix was never actually exercised in CI until PR #35 re-enabled the job, confirmed via 4 consecutive clean CI passes. Along the way also: added an HTML reporter to `playwright.config.js` (every project except `p0` had been silently producing an empty `playwright-report/` — CI failures were undebuggable from artifacts alone); fixed a webpack-build-race (`wait-on` only confirms the port is open, not that the client bundle finished compiling — added a step polling `dev-server.log` for `webpack built client`); fixed the original missing-Commerce-API-env-vars bug (job now binds `environment: dev`, sources `COMMERCE_API_*` from `vars.*`, `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`'s `push <tier>` uploads a shared+tier merge so one environment binding is self-sufficient); switched the job gate from `always()` to `!cancelled()` so a superseded/cancelled run doesn't burn a 15-min runner slot.
- PR #30 (`feature/gh-qa-workflow`, merged) also: deleted the unfinished `SFCC-000_guest-checkout` placeholder (never had real Adyen payment interaction, self-described `EXAMPLE` in its own header) and its `testIgnore` mis-scoping (ran under `chromium`/`mobile-chrome` `retries:2` instead of the dedicated `p0` project's `retries:0`, costing ~12 of the ~14 min `e2e-localhost` runtime on every PR); added a homepage smoke test (new `homepage` E2E area + `SMOKE-` naming convention for Jira-less tests); fixed a `@typescript-eslint/no-var-requires` misconfiguration flagging `require()` in `e2e/`'s intentionally-CommonJS files; added `test-results/`/`playwright-report/` to `.gitignore`.
- **Proposed: tag-based environment promotion (GitFlow) — full spec on Confluence, implementation not yet started.** Full rationale, tag naming convention, worked commands, and open questions:
  [Proposed: Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/335216656/Proposed+Tag-Based+Environment+Promotion+GitFlow)
  (Confluence, v5, child of the Branching Guide page). Summary: only `Dev` should be continuously tied to `develop`; every other tier should deploy a specific, immutable git tag (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N` / `vX.Y.Z` / `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`, cut via `npm version`) instead of a branch ref, so Test/SIT/UAT/Stage can each run independent testing cycles instead of being forced onto the same moving branch. **Do not implement the AGENTS.md/governance pieces without squad-lead + Integration-lead sign-off — this is still a proposal.** Implementation checklist for a fresh session on a new branch (see the Confluence page for full detail on each item):
  - **Decided 2026-07-16** (see Confluence page's "Decisions made so far" table): release cadence is per-sprint; pre-launch versioning starts at `v0.1.0` (MAJOR locked at `0` until go-live, which becomes `v1.0.0`); `Test` gets its own automated CI gate (not manual-only); tag protection + the version-guard + Release-per-final-tag are all adopted immediately, not phased in.
  - **Tooling — safe to build now, doesn't touch governance docs:**
    1. `npm version` adoption — no code change needed, it's a built-in npm command; just start using it per the Confluence page's "How to deploy" section instead of raw `git tag`. First tag will be `v0.1.0-rc.0`.
    2. **Primary enforcement — one GitHub Ruleset covers both naming and immutability:** Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New tag ruleset, targeting `v*`, with a "tag name pattern" rule requiring `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$` plus "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled. This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com). Keep a `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow too, as defense-in-depth / for a clearer failure message than the raw ruleset rejection gives.
    3. A version-guard step added to each `deploy-*.yml` (test/sit/stg/uat/prod) — fetch the environment's current deployed tag via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=<env>`, semver-compare against the tag being deployed (use the `semver` npm package, not hand-rolled bash comparison — pre-release identifiers must be dot-separated, e.g. `-rc.10` vs `-rc.2`, or numeric comparison breaks), fail on a downgrade. **`<env>` must be the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; we hit this exact mismatch once already this session, commit `12bf91b`). Map each tier explicitly (`stg` → `staging`, everything else matches its filename) rather than deriving it from the filename. Fail closed if the environment name is wrong or the API call errors — a genuine first-ever deployment (no prior Deployment record at all) is fine to proceed, but an unresolvable environment/API error is not the same thing and must not be treated as "nothing to compare against, allow it."
    4. **A Test-tier CI gate** — new, decided 2026-07-16. Proposed shape (not yet confirmed, see the page's remaining two open questions): a second job appended to `deploy-test.yml` that runs a P0-only Playwright suite against whatever was just deployed, so the run's pass/fail becomes the "safe to promote to SIT" signal — deliberately deploy-then-gate rather than SIT Gate's gate-then-deploy, since `Test` is on-demand (`workflow_dispatch`, including raw feature branches) and has no push/PR event to hang a pre-check on.
    5. Wire `/generate-changelog`'s existing `gh release create` offer into the "cut the final tag" step — no new tooling, the skill already does this.
  - **Governance — needs squad-lead + Integration-lead review before merging:**
    6. A new `.claude/rules/tagging.md` (or fold into `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, already auto-loaded on `release/*`/`hotfix/*`) documenting the tag convention and instructing Claude to always use `npm version`, never hand-construct a tag string.
    7. `AGENTS.md`'s branch table / the Confluence Branching Guide itself, once the team has actually reviewed and approved the proposal — this repo's `AGENTS.md` requires both squad leads and the Integration lead to sign off on changes to itself, stronger than the usual verified-session Tier 1 exception.
  - Still open per the Confluence page: exact Test-gate design (deploy-then-gate as proposed, or match SIT's gate-then-deploy exactly) and its scope (P0 suite only, or also bundle-size/contract-tests/Lighthouse).

## Unresolved Dependencies
Do not hard-code assumptions for the following — ask the user before implementing:
- Product copy ownership: Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21 (TBD).
- Translation trigger workflow with TransPerfect (TBD).
- Global-e + Didomi consent interaction (TBD).
- **Social login (Apple/Google):** Confirmed in scope for launch (ENH-004, Must-Have, Go-Live) as SFCC OOTB configuration only. **Hard dependency:** Apple and Google merchant accounts must be provisioned by Zimmermann before implementation can start. Do not implement until merchant accounts exist.
- **Omneo guest record creation timing:** When to create an Omneo record for a guest (at newsletter sign-up, at back-in-stock capture, at checkout, or only at order completion) is under legal/SFCC best-practice review. SFCC best practice is order completion only. Do not create Omneo records for guests at any earlier point until confirmed. Note: CRM-012–015 are signed off but Tony Tilbrook (early creation) and Izzy Coxon (order-completion only) currently disagree on the timing — treat as Open until reconciled.
- **Denmark routing:** Which storefront Denmark resolves to is not yet confirmed.
- **EU billing fields:** Locale-specific billing fields (Italian Codice Fiscale, Spanish NIF, French SIRET) — to be confirmed before implementing.
- **Adyen dynamic checkout (ENH-020):** Confirmed Must-Have for Go-Live, but a **hard dependency on Adyen** delivering A/B-able dynamic payment-method display. Do not assume the feature is buildable end-to-end until Adyen delivery is confirmed.
- **Optimizely SFCC data-layer scope (AAB-004):** Load mechanism Confirmed (PWA-direct head tag, US-only, Zimmermann-provided script). Residual: Tell No Lies suspects no SFCC-side data-layer work is needed for Optimizely (Magento launch was GTM-only). Confirm with Tell No Lies before doing SFCC data-layer work specifically for Optimizely.
- **CRM-155 customer group precedence:** Rules for resolving overlapping customer group memberships are TBD.
- **Mulesoft stock aggregation (CAI-023):** Confirmation pending that Mulesoft can aggregate warehouse + boutique stock pre-checkout.

Confirm which sheet is authoritative before relying on Einstein for cart/recommendation surfaces.

- **Addingwell role in analytics (AAB-001/003):** AAB-001 frames all container/tag logic as living in GTM (Tell No Lies), while the Third Party Integrations rows say the GTM container loads *via the Addingwell MRT integration* and GA4/downstream tags route through an Addingwell *server-side container*. Reconciled in analytics.md as logic-vs-transport, but confirm with Tell No Lies whether Addingwell is none / transport-only / server-side routing.
- **DMU-007 order history source (upstream):** DMU-007 PWA contract Confirmed (displays MuleSoft payload). Residual upstream conflict: requirement + JT say NewStore via MuleSoft; RJ says "Order history will come from Omneo." Out of PWA boundary — reconcile so the integration contract is unambiguous.

My Account profile pages must round-trip to Omneo post-auth. Graceful degradation for Omneo outages on account screens is now load-bearing — confirm UX before implementing profile reads.

Separately, the source note now records the platform CDN as Akamai (SFCC default), which sits against existing Cloudflare carry-forward references — confirm the CDN platform of record (no asset-migration impact either way).

A SFCC-hosted wishlist for go-live is being scoped but NOT confirmed. ENH-040 still logs an eventual SFCC→Omneo migration. Note: Move-to-Wishlist (CAI-004/008) is **confirmed authenticated-only** at launch — guests are prompted to log in; guest wishlist is a logged enhancement out of scope for go-live.

Hard dependency: the delivery completion date must be passed back via MuleSoft.

Can this be reviewed?" — broader address-validity enhancement, unscoped.

- **Proposed: tag-based environment promotion (GitFlow) — full spec on Confluence, implementation not yet started.** Full rationale, tag naming convention, worked commands, and open questions:
  [Proposed: Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/335216656/Proposed+Tag-Based+Environment+Promotion+GitFlow)
  (Confluence, v5, child of the Branching Guide page). Summary: only `Dev` should be continuously tied to `develop`; every other tier should deploy a specific, immutable git tag (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N` / `vX.Y.Z` / `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`, cut via `npm version`) instead of a branch ref, so Test/SIT/UAT/Stage can each run independent testing cycles instead of being forced onto the same moving branch. **Do not implement the AGENTS.md/governance pieces without squad-lead + Integration-lead sign-off — this is still a proposal.** Implementation checklist for a fresh session on a new branch (see the Confluence page for full detail on each item):
  - **Decided 2026-07-16** (see Confluence page's "Decisions made so far" table): release cadence is per-sprint; pre-launch versioning starts at `v0.1.0` (MAJOR locked at `0` until go-live, which becomes `v1.0.0`); `Test` gets its own automated CI gate (not manual-only); tag protection + the version-guard + Release-per-final-tag are all adopted immediately, not phased in.
  - **Tooling — safe to build now, doesn't touch governance docs:**
    1. `npm version` adoption — no code change needed, it's a built-in npm command; just start using it per the Confluence page's "How to deploy" section instead of raw `git tag`. First tag will be `v0.1.0-rc.0`.
    2. **Primary enforcement — one GitHub Ruleset covers both naming and immutability:** Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New tag ruleset, targeting `v*`, with a "tag name pattern" rule requiring `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$` plus "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled. This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com). Keep a `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow too, as defense-in-depth / for a clearer failure message than the raw ruleset rejection gives.
    3. A version-guard step added to each `deploy-*.yml` (test/sit/stg/uat/prod) — fetch the environment's current deployed tag via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=<env>`, semver-compare against the tag being deployed (use the `semver` npm package, not hand-rolled bash comparison — pre-release identifiers must be dot-separated, e.g. `-rc.10` vs `-rc.2`, or numeric comparison breaks), fail on a downgrade. **`<env>` must be the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; we hit this exact mismatch once already this session, commit `12bf91b`). Map each tier explicitly (`stg` → `staging`, everything else matches its filename) rather than deriving it from the filename. Fail closed if the environment name is wrong or the API call errors — a genuine first-ever deployment (no prior Deployment record at all) is fine to proceed, but an unresolvable environment/API error is not the same thing and must not be treated as "nothing to compare against, allow it."
    4. **A Test-tier CI gate** — new, decided 2026-07-16. Proposed shape (not yet confirmed, see the page's remaining two open questions): a second job appended to `deploy-test.yml` that runs a P0-only Playwright suite against whatever was just deployed, so the run's pass/fail becomes the "safe to promote to SIT" signal — deliberately deploy-then-gate rather than SIT Gate's gate-then-deploy, since `Test` is on-demand (`workflow_dispatch`, including raw feature branches) and has no push/PR event to hang a pre-check on.
    5. Wire `/generate-changelog`'s existing `gh release create` offer into the "cut the final tag" step — no new tooling, the skill already does this.
  - **Governance — needs squad-lead + Integration-lead review before merging:**
    6. A new `.claude/rules/tagging.md` (or fold into `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, already auto-loaded on `release/*`/`hotfix/*`) documenting the tag convention and instructing Claude to always use `npm version`, never hand-construct a tag string.
    7. `AGENTS.md`'s branch table / the Confluence Branching Guide itself, once the team has actually reviewed and approved the proposal — this repo's `AGENTS.md` requires both squad leads and the Integration lead to sign off on changes to itself, stronger than the usual verified-session Tier 1 exception.
  - Still open per the Confluence page: exact Test-gate design (deploy-then-gate as proposed, or match SIT's gate-then-deploy exactly) and its scope (P0 suite only, or also bundle-size/contract-tests/Lighthouse).

=== 3. doc references — §60, §3 diagram, §4 CPA row, §9 L128 ===
# 02 — Contentful (CMS)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Contentful is the headless CMS for editorial content: homepage modules, promotional banners, lookbooks, campaign landing pages, size guide fallback content (primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay — PRD-053), footer, and editorial blocks on PLPs and PDPs. The storefront reads published content via the **Delivery API (CDA)** from both SSR and the browser, reads draft content via the **Preview API (CPA)** in editor sessions, and receives **publish webhooks** to clear the SSR cache.

In scope:

- Reading published content via the Delivery API
- Reading draft content via the Preview API in editor preview sessions
...
        │        on dev/test/sit/uat only (never staging or prod).
        │        Reached client-side on the /preview route and via
        │        ?preview on Experience pages — both are gated: if no
        │        CPA token is present the routes fall back to a 404 /
        │        delivery mode. The Live Preview SDK requires the token
        │        in the browser for postMessage-based real-time updates.
        │
        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
        │
        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
---
- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.

## 4. Authentication and credentials

| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|
| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
| Preview API token (CPA) | `/preview` route and `?preview` on Experience pages (dev/test/sit/uat only — never staging or prod) | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. Set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only; never set on staging or prod. The `/preview` route returns 404 when token absent; Experience pages with `?preview` fall back to Delivery API mode. Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (required for postMessage updates). |
| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |
---

## 9. Security and privacy

- The CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment. Embedding in the bundle is safe per Contentful's published guidance.
- The CPA token is set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only — never on staging or prod. It reaches the browser on the `/preview` route (which returns 404 when no token is present) and `?preview` Experience pages (which fall back to Delivery API mode when no token is present). Both preview paths are `noindex` and not linked from any storefront navigation. This is a deliberate tradeoff: the Live Preview SDK requires the token client-side for real-time postMessage updates, and the non-prod-only gate means the token is never in a production bundle.
- The CMA token is held only on the CI host — never embedded, never in PR diffs.
- No PII is handled by Contentful.

## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation

72:- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the `/preview` route renders the entry inside Studio's iframe. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK subscribes to `postMessage` events from Studio for real-time content updates. The CPA token is used client-side here — this is required by the SDK and is acceptable because: (a) the token is only set on dev/test/sit/uat only (never staging or prod) MRT environments, (b) the route returns a 404 when no preview token is present, and (c) the route is `noindex`. The MRT proxy approach was considered but deferred in favour of the simpler client-side SDK integration.

Set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only; never set on staging or prod. The `/preview` route returns 404 when token absent; Experience pages with `?preview` fall back to Delivery API mode. Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (required for postMessage updates). |
120:| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
128:- The CPA token is set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only — never on staging or prod. It reaches the browser on the `/preview` route (which returns 404 when no token is present) and `?preview` Experience pages (which fall back to Delivery API mode when no token is present). Both preview paths are `noindex` and not linked from any storefront navigation. This is a deliberate tradeoff: the Live Preview SDK requires the token client-side for real-time postMessage updates, and the non-prod-only gate means the token is never in a production bundle.

2	import type {ContentfulClientApi} from 'contentful'
3	import Seo from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/seo'
4	import {useLocation} from 'react-router-dom'
5	import {Box, Spinner, Text} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui'
6	import {createClient} from 'contentful'
7	import {ExperienceRoot, useFetchBySlug} from '@contentful/experiences-sdk-react'
8	import {ContentfulLivePreviewProvider} from '@contentful/live-preview/react'
9	import useMultiSite from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-multi-site'
10	import {
11	    getContentfulConfig,
12	    CONTENTFUL_FALLBACK_LOCALE,
13	    CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_HOST,
14	    CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_HOST,
15	    CONTENTFUL_LIVE_PREVIEW_ORIGIN,
16	} from '../../config/contentful'
17	
18	// Side-effect import — registers experience components with the Contentful Experiences SDK (cached, so this is fine)
19	import '../../components/contentful/experiences/definitions'
20	
21	const EXPERIENCE_TYPE_ID = 'collectionPageExp'
22	
23	type ExperienceFetchProps = {
24	    // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
25	    client: ContentfulClientApi<any>
26	    slug: string
27	    locale: string
28	    isPreview: boolean
29	}
30	
31	/** Inner component so useFetchBySlug is always called unconditionally at the top level. */
32	const ExperienceFetch = ({client, slug, locale, isPreview}: ExperienceFetchProps) => {
33	    // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
34	    const {experience, isLoading, error} = useFetchBySlug({
35	        client: client as any,
36	        slug,
37	        experienceTypeId: EXPERIENCE_TYPE_ID,
38	        localeCode: locale,
39	    })
40	
41	    if (isLoading) {
42	        return (
43	            <Box p={8} display="flex" justifyContent="center">
44	                <Spinner size="xl" />
45	            </Box>
46	        )
47	    }
48	
49	    if (error || !experience) {
50	        return (
51	            <Box p={8}>
52	                <Text color="red.500">Page not found.</Text>
53	            </Box>
54	        )
55	    }
56	
57	    const root = <ExperienceRoot experience={experience} locale={locale} />
58	
59	    if (isPreview) {
60	        return (
61	            <>
62	                {/* noindex — preview mode serves draft content, must not be indexed */}
63	                <Seo noIndex />
64	                <ContentfulLivePreviewProvider
65	                    locale={locale}
66	                    enableInspectorMode={true}
67	                    enableLiveUpdates={true}
68	                    targetOrigin={CONTENTFUL_LIVE_PREVIEW_ORIGIN}
69	                >
70	                    {root}
71	                </ContentfulLivePreviewProvider>
72	            </>
73	        )
74	    }
75	
76	    return root
77	}
78	
79	type ExperiencePageProps = {
80	    slug: string
81	    isPreview?: boolean
82	}
83	
84	const ExperiencePage = ({slug, isPreview = false}: ExperiencePageProps) => {
85	    const {locale: siteLocale} = useMultiSite() as {locale?: {id: string}}
86	    const locale = siteLocale?.id || CONTENTFUL_FALLBACK_LOCALE
87	    const {spaceId, environment, previewAccessToken, accessToken} = getContentfulConfig() ?? {}
88	    const previewUnavailable = isPreview && !previewAccessToken
89	    // Use preview host only when explicitly in preview mode AND a preview token is available.
90	    // Falls back to delivery mode silently when no token is set (non-prod gate).
91	    const effectivePreview = isPreview && !!previewAccessToken
92	    const token = effectivePreview ? previewAccessToken : accessToken
93	    const host = effectivePreview ? CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_HOST : CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_HOST
94	
95	    const client = useMemo(() => {
96	        if (!spaceId || !token) return null
97	        return createClient({space: spaceId, environment, accessToken: token, host})
98	    }, [spaceId, environment, token, host])
99	
100	    if (previewUnavailable) {
101	        return (
102	            <Box p={8}>
103	                <Text color="red.500">
104	                    Preview is not enabled in this environment.
105	                </Text>
106	            </Box>
107	        )
108	    }
109	
110	    if (!client) {
111	        return (
112	            <Box p={8}>
113	                <Text color="red.500">Contentful configuration is missing — cannot render this page.</Text>
114	            </Box>
115	        )
116	    }
117	
118	    return <ExperienceFetch client={client} slug={slug} locale={locale} isPreview={effectivePreview} />
119	}
120	
121	const Experience = () => {
122	    const {pathname, search} = useLocation()
123	    const slug = pathname.slice(1) // strip leading '/'
124	    const isPreview = new URLSearchParams(search).has('preview')
125	
126	    return <ExperiencePage slug={slug} isPreview={isPreview} />
127	}
128	
129	Experience.getTemplateName = () => 'experience';
130	
131	export default Experience;

content.content:
1	# 02 — Contentful (CMS)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Contentful is the headless CMS for editorial content: homepage modules, promotional banners, lookbooks, campaign landing pages, size guide fallback content (primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay — PRD-053), footer, and editorial blocks on PLPs and PDPs. The storefront reads published content via the **Delivery API (CDA)** from both SSR and the browser, reads draft content via the **Preview API (CPA)** in editor sessions, and receives **publish webhooks** to clear the SSR cache.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- Reading published content via the Delivery API
10	- Reading draft content via the Preview API in editor preview sessions
11	- Live preview in Contentful Studio
12	- Locale-specific content via Contentful's native localisation
13	- Contentful Studio Experiences — drag-and-drop page composition by editors
14	- Receiving publish webhooks to clear stale SSR cache entries
15	
16	Out of scope of this document:
17	
18	- Content type schema sync (managed in code via the Management API — see §2)
19	- Asset uploads and content editing in Contentful Studio
20	- Webhooks from Contentful to SFCC (none planned)
21	
22	**Content ownership.** SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001). Rows marked *pending* are unconfirmed (see §11).
23	
24	| Surface | SFCC owns | Contentful owns | Status |
25	|---|---|---|---|
26	| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
27	| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
28	| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
29	| Size guides | — | Fallback content only — primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay (PRD-053, confirmed 2026-06-19); Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product | Updated |
30	| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
31	| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
32	| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
33	| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |
34	| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005); clickable badges link to category/PLP. Contentful is not the source of badge content unless explicitly confirmed. | — | Confirmed |
35	
36	## 2. Content type management (build-time)
37	
38	Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:
39	
40	- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
41	- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
42	- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.
43	
44	## 3. Browser-side architecture
45	
46	```
47	PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
48	        │
49	        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
50	        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
51	        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
52	        │
53	        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
54	        │        Editor preview only. Token held server-side in MRT;
55	        │        never reaches the browser. Requests proxied through
56	        │        an MRT preview endpoint.
57	        │
58	        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
59	        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
60	        │
61	        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
62	                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
63	                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
64	```
65	
66	- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
67	- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
68	- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the storefront renders inside Studio's iframe. It detects the preview origin, switches to the CPA-backed MRT proxy, and refreshes on `postMessage` events from Studio.
69	- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.
70	
71	## 4. Authentication and credentials
72	
73	| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
74	|---|---|---|
75	| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
76	| Preview API token (CPA) | MRT preview proxy only | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. MRT environment variable. Never reaches the browser. |
77	| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
78	| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |
79	
80	Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.
81	
82	## 5. Data exchanged
83	
84	| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
85	|---|---|---|
86	| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
87	| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
88	| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
89	| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
90	| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |
91	
92	No PII flows through Contentful.
93	
94	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
95	
96	- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
97	- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
98	- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
99	- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
100	- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
101	- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.
102	
103	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
104	
105	- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
