# 02 — Contentful (CMS)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Contentful is the headless CMS for editorial content: homepage modules, promotional banners, lookbooks, campaign landing pages, size guide fallback content (primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay — PRD-053), footer, and editorial blocks on PLPs and PDPs. The storefront reads published content via the **Delivery API (CDA)** from both SSR and the browser, reads draft content via the **Preview API (CPA)** in editor sessions, and receives **publish webhooks** to clear the SSR cache.

In scope:

- Reading published content via the Delivery API
- Reading draft content via the Preview API in editor preview sessions
- Live preview in Contentful Studio
- Locale-specific content via Contentful's native localisation
- Contentful Studio Experiences — drag-and-drop page composition by editors
- Receiving publish webhooks to clear stale SSR cache entries

Out of scope of this document:

- Content type schema sync (managed in code via the Management API — see §2)
- Asset uploads and content editing in Contentful Studio
- Webhooks from Contentful to SFCC (none planned)

**Content ownership.** SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001). Rows marked *pending* are unconfirmed (see §11).

| Surface | SFCC owns | Contentful owns | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
| Size guides | — | Fallback content only — primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay (PRD-053, confirmed 2026-06-19); Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product | Updated |
| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |
| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005); clickable badges link to category/PLP. Contentful is not the source of badge content unless explicitly confirmed. | — | Confirmed |

## 2. Content type management (build-time)

Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:

- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.

## 3. Browser-side architecture

```
PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
        │
        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
        │
        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
        │        Editor preview only. Token held server-side in MRT;
        │        never reaches the browser. Requests proxied through
        │        an MRT preview endpoint.
        │
        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
        │
        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
```

- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the storefront renders inside Studio's iframe. It detects the preview origin, switches to the CPA-backed MRT proxy, and refreshes on `postMessage` events from Studio.
- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.

## 4. Authentication and credentials

| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|
| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
| Preview API token (CPA) | MRT preview proxy only | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. MRT environment variable. Never reaches the browser. |
| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |

Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.

## 5. Data exchanged

| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |

No PII flows through Contentful.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.

## 7. Multi-region behaviour

- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.

## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |

## 9. Security and privacy

- The CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment. Embedding in the bundle is safe per Contentful's published guidance.
- The CPA token is held server-side only and is never logged.
- The CMA token is held only on the CI host — never embedded, never in PR diffs.
- No PII is handled by Contentful.

## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC owns all commerce data, Contentful owns editorial. Not yet confirmed is the split on composed pages: which editorial blocks appear on PDP and PLP, whether they are authored in SFCC Page Designer or Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or built in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu includes Contentful-authored promotional tiles. The working assumption is in the ownership table in §1.
3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provide per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be tested against a real Contentful environment.

**6 files have lint errors, but only 4 are in our PR.** Two are **not ours**:

content.content:
40	- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
41	- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
42	- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.
43	
44	## 3. Browser-side architecture
45	
46	```
47	PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
48	        │
49	        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
50	        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
51	        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
52	        │
53	        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
54	        │        Editor preview only. Token set in MRT as an env var
55	        │        on dev/test/sit/uat only (never staging or prod).
56	        │        Reached client-side on the /preview route and via
57	        │        ?preview on Experience pages — both are gated: if no
58	        │        CPA token is present the routes fall back to a 404 /
59	        │        delivery mode. The Live Preview SDK requires the token
60	        │        in the browser for postMessage-based real-time updates.
61	        │
62	        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
63	        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
64	        │
65	        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
66	                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
67	                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
68	```
69	
70	- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
71	- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
72	- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the `/preview` route renders the entry inside Studio's iframe. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK subscribes to `postMessage` events from Studio for real-time content updates. The CPA token is used client-side here — this is required by the SDK and is acceptable because: (a) the token is only set on dev/test/sit/uat only (never staging or prod) MRT environments, (b) the route returns a 404 when no preview token is present, and (c) the route is `noindex`. The MRT proxy approach was considered but deferred in favour of the simpler client-side SDK integration.
73	- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.
74	
75	## 4. Authentication and credentials
76	
77	| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
78	|---|---|---|
79	| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
80	| Preview API token (CPA) | `/preview` route and `?preview` on Experience pages (dev/test/sit/uat only — never staging or prod) | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. Set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only; never set on staging or prod. The `/preview` route returns 404 when token absent; Experience pages with `?preview` fall back to Delivery API mode. Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (required for postMessage updates). |
81	| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
82	| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |
83	
84	Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.
85	
86	## 5. Data exchanged
87	
88	| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
89	|---|---|---|
90	| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
91	| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
92	| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
93	| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
94	| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |
95	
96	No PII flows through Contentful.
97	
98	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
99	
100	- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
101	- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
102	- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
103	- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
104	- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
105	- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.
106

file.content:
- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.

## 3. Browser-side architecture

```
PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
        │
        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
        │
        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
        │        Editor preview only. Token set in MRT as an env var
        │        on dev/test/sit/uat only (never staging or prod).
        │        Reached client-side on the /preview route and via
        │        ?preview on Experience pages — both are gated: if no
        │        CPA token is present the routes fall back to a 404 /
        │        delivery mode. The Live Preview SDK requires the token
        │        in the browser for postMessage-based real-time updates.
        │
        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
        │
        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
```

- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the `/preview` route renders the entry inside Studio's iframe. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK subscribes to `postMessage` events from Studio for real-time content updates. The CPA token is used client-side here — this is required by the SDK and is acceptable because: (a) the token is only set on dev/test/sit/uat only (never staging or prod) MRT environments, (b) the route returns a 404 when no preview token is present, and (c) the route is `noindex`. The MRT proxy approach was considered but deferred in favour of the simpler client-side SDK integration.
- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.

## 4. Authentication and credentials

| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|
| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
| Preview API token (CPA) | `/preview` route and `?preview` on Experience pages (dev/test/sit/uat only — never staging or prod) | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. Set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only; never set on staging or prod. The `/preview` route returns 404 when token absent; Experience pages with `?preview` fall back to Delivery API mode. Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (required for postMessage updates). |
| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |

Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.

## 5. Data exchanged

| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |

No PII flows through Contentful.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.

## 7. Multi-region behaviour

- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.

## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |

## 9. Security and privacy

- The CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment. Embedding in the bundle is safe per Contentful's published guidance.
- The CPA token is set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only — never on staging or prod. It reaches the browser on the `/preview` route (which returns 404 when no token is present) and `?preview` Experience pages (which fall back to Delivery API mode when no token is present). Both preview paths are `noindex` and not linked from any storefront navigation. This is a deliberate tradeoff: the Live Preview SDK requires the token client-side for real-time postMessage updates, and the non-prod-only gate means the token is never in a production bundle.
- The CMA token is held only on the CI host — never embedded, never in PR diffs.
- No PII is handled by Contentful.

## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.

There's already an `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` — but it's **REST-based** (`useContentfulEntry`/`useContentfulEntries` via raw `fetch`). ### A. NEW — `overrides/app/hooks/useContentfulClient.ts` (the DRY should-fix) · Tier 4
Centralises the `getContentfulConfig() → useMemo(createClient)` block **and the CPA-token gate**, so `/preview` and `?preview` can't drift again. Written prettier-compliant from the start (2-space/semi). Proposed interface:

```tsx
type UseContentfulClientResult = {
  client: ContentfulClientApi<any> | null;   // eslint-disable-line — matches existing usage
  previewUnavailable: boolean;  // preview requested but no CPA token → caller must 404 + noindex
  isPreview: boolean;           // actually in preview (requested AND token present)
};

export function useContentfulClient({preview = false}: {preview?: boolean} = {}): UseContentfulClientResult
```
The gate logic (`previewUnavailable`, `isPreview`, token/host selection) lives here once. **JSDoc + `@returns`** per hook conventions.

### B. NEW — `overrides/app/hooks/useContentfulClient.test.ts` · Tier 4

The `previewUnavailable` branch becomes a real 404 + noindex, matching `/preview`:

```tsx
const {res} = useServerContext();
const {client, previewUnavailable, isPreview: effectivePreview} = useContentfulClient({preview: isPreview});

if (previewUnavailable) {
  if (res) res.status(404);
  return (
    <>
      <Seo noIndex />
      <Box p={8}><Text color="red.500">Preview is not enabled in this environment.</Text></Box>

```

1	# 02 — Contentful (CMS)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Contentful is the headless CMS for editorial content: homepage modules, promotional banners, lookbooks, campaign landing pages, size guide fallback content (primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay — PRD-053), footer, and editorial blocks on PLPs and PDPs. The storefront reads published content via the **Delivery API (CDA)** from both SSR and the browser, reads draft content via the **Preview API (CPA)** in editor sessions, and receives **publish webhooks** to clear the SSR cache.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- Reading published content via the Delivery API
10	- Reading draft content via the Preview API in editor preview sessions
11	- Live preview in Contentful Studio
12	- Locale-specific content via Contentful's native localisation
13	- Contentful Studio Experiences — drag-and-drop page composition by editors
14	- Receiving publish webhooks to clear stale SSR cache entries
15	
16	Out of scope of this document:
17	
18	- Content type schema sync (managed in code via the Management API — see §2)
19	- Asset uploads and content editing in Contentful Studio
20	- Webhooks from Contentful to SFCC (none planned)
21	
22	**Content ownership.** SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001). Rows marked *pending* are unconfirmed (see §11).
23	
24	| Surface | SFCC owns | Contentful owns | Status |
25	|---|---|---|---|
26	| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
27	| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
28	| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
29	| Size guides | — | Fallback content only — primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay (PRD-053, confirmed 2026-06-19); Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product | Updated |
30	| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
31	| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
32	| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
33	| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |
34	| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005); clickable badges link to category/PLP. Contentful is not the source of badge content unless explicitly confirmed. | — | Confirmed |
35	
36	## 2. Content type management (build-time)
37	
38	Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:
39	
40	- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
41	- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
42	- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.
43	
44	## 3. Browser-side architecture
45	
46	```
47	PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
48	        │
49	        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
50	        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
51	        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
52	        │
53	        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
54	        │        Editor preview only. Token set in MRT as an env var
55	        │        on dev/test/sit/uat only (never staging or prod).
56	        │        Reached client-side on the /preview route and via
57	        │        ?preview on Experience pages — both are gated: if no
58	        │        CPA token is present the routes fall back to a 404 /
59	        │        delivery mode. The Live Preview SDK requires the token
60	        │        in the browser for postMessage-based real-time updates.
61	        │
62	        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
63	        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
64	        │
65	        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
66	                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
67	                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
68	```
69	
70	- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
71	- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
72	- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the `/preview` route renders the entry inside Studio's iframe. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK subscribes to `postMessage` events from Studio for real-time content updates. The CPA token is used client-side here — this is required by the SDK and is acceptable because: (a) the token is only set on dev/test/sit/uat only (never staging or prod) MRT environments, (b) the route returns a 404 when no preview token is present, and (c) the route is `noindex`. The MRT proxy approach was considered but deferred in favour of the simpler client-side SDK integration.
73	- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.
74	
75	## 4. Authentication and credentials
76	
77	| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
78	|---|---|---|
79	| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
80	| Preview API token (CPA) | `/preview` route and `?preview` on Experience pages (dev/test/sit/uat only — never staging or prod) | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. Set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only; never set on staging or prod. The `/preview` route returns 404 when token absent; Experience pages with `?preview` fall back to Delivery API mode. 89	|---|---|---|
90	| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
91	| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
92	| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |

100	- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.

1	# 02 — Contentful (CMS)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Contentful is the headless CMS for editorial content: homepage modules, promotional banners, lookbooks, campaign landing pages, size guide fallback content (primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay — PRD-053), footer, and editorial blocks on PLPs and PDPs. The storefront reads published content via the **Delivery API (CDA)** from both SSR and the browser, reads draft content via the **Preview API (CPA)** in editor sessions, and receives **publish webhooks** to clear the SSR cache.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- Reading published content via the Delivery API
10	- Reading draft content via the Preview API in editor preview sessions
11	- Live preview in Contentful Studio
12	- Locale-specific content via Contentful's native localisation
13	- Contentful Studio Experiences — drag-and-drop page composition by editors
14	- Receiving publish webhooks to clear stale SSR cache entries
15	
16	Out of scope of this document:
17	
18	- Content type schema sync (managed in code via the Management API — see §2)
19	- Asset uploads and content editing in Contentful Studio
20	- Webhooks from Contentful to SFCC (none planned)
21	
22	**Content ownership.** SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001). Rows marked *pending* are unconfirmed (see §11).
23	
24	| Surface | SFCC owns | Contentful owns | Status |
25	|---|---|---|---|
26	| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
27	| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
28	| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
29	| Size guides | — | Fallback content only — primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay (PRD-053, confirmed 2026-06-19); Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product | Updated |
30	| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
31	| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
32	| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
33	| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |
34	| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005); clickable badges link to category/PLP. Contentful is not the source of badge content unless explicitly confirmed. | — | Confirmed |
35	
36	## 2. Content type management (build-time)
37	
38	Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:
39	
40	- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
41	- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
42	- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.
43	
44	## 3. Browser-side architecture
45	
46	```
47	PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
48	        │
49	        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
50	        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
51	        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
52	        │
53	        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
54	        │        Editor preview only. Token set in MRT as an env var
55	        │        on dev/test/sit/uat only (never staging or prod).
56	        │        Reached client-side on the /preview route and via
57	        │        ?preview on Experience pages — both are gated: if no
58	        │        CPA token is present the routes fall back to a 404 /
59	        │        delivery mode. The Live Preview SDK requires the token
60	        │        in the browser for postMessage-based real-time updates.
61	        │
62	        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
63	        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
64	        │
65	        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
66	                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
67	                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
68	```
69	
70	- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
71	- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
72	- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the `/preview` route renders the entry inside Studio's iframe. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK subscribes to `postMessage` events from Studio for real-time content updates. The CPA token is used client-side here — this is required by the SDK and is acceptable because: (a) the token is only set on dev/test/sit/uat only (never staging or prod) MRT environments, (b) the route returns a 404 when no preview token is present, and (c) the route is `noindex`. The MRT proxy approach was considered but deferred in favour of the simpler client-side SDK integration.
73	- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.
74	
75	## 4. Authentication and credentials
76	
77	| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
78	|---|---|---|
79	| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
80	| Preview API token (CPA) | `/preview` route and `?preview` on Experience pages (dev/test/sit/uat only — never staging or prod) | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. Set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only; never set on staging or prod. The `/preview` route returns 404 when token absent; Experience pages with `?preview` fall back to Delivery API mode. Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (required for postMessage updates). |
81	| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
82	| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |
83	
84	Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.
85	
86	## 5. Data exchanged
87	
88	| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
89	|---|---|---|
90	| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
91	| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
92	| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
93	| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
94	| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |
95	
96	No PII flows through Contentful.
97	
98	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
99	
100	- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
101	- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.

Audit code quality for the specified scope. Do not modify any files — this is a read-only

The user will provide one of:

## Parallel execution

For audits covering more than 5 files, split into four independent checks and run them
as parallel agents simultaneously. Each agent receives only its own checklist — do not
bundle all checks into one agent.

- **Agent A — Naming & structure**
- **Agent B — Import analysis**
- **Agent C — TypeScript coverage**
- **Agent D — Test & story coverage**

For 5 files or fewer, run all checks sequentially in a single pass.

---

## Agent A — Naming & structure

Rules are defined once, split across [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md)
(cross-cutting), [css.md](../../rules/css.md) (Chakra/styling), and
[components.md](../../rules/components.md) (components/hooks/Storybook) — read the relevant

that's how the files drift apart.

Walk the file list and audit each file against the relevant section:

- Every file → conventions.md **General** section.
- Every file with JSX/Chakra props → css.md **Tokens** section (no hardcoded hex/px values).
- `.tsx` under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/` → components.md
  **Components** + **Composition** sections, plus conventions.md **File naming and folder
  structure**.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/hooks/` → components.md **Hooks** section.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/utils/` → conventions.md **Utilities** section.

For each violation, record `file:line` and which rule file + bullet failed — the section
anchor is enough (e.g. "components.md → Components → Props type placement").

---

## Agent B — Import analysis

For each file, read the import statements and check:

- No circular imports: if File A imports from File B, File B must not import from File A
  (check by reading the imported file's imports in turn — one level deep is sufficient).
- No imports from a higher tier without justification:
  - A component must not import directly from internal `commerce-sdk-react` source paths.
  - A page must not bypass its own hooks to call raw API functions.
- No imports from a later-sprint feature (reference `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` when present).
- No `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels — flag for path alias review.

---

## Agent C — TypeScript coverage

Check each file against the relevant rule file:

- Every `.ts`/`.tsx` → [typescript.md](../../rules/typescript.md) in full (no `any` without
  justification, `type` vs `interface`, non-null assertions, discriminated unions, utility
  types, `import type`, `satisfies`, `readonly`, generic naming).
- Components → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Components** (props type name,
  placement, optional `?`, callback naming, JSDoc).
- Hooks → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Hooks** (typed params, explicit
  return type, JSDoc with `@returns`).

Then run `npx tsc --noEmit` **once** for the whole branch (not per file) and report any
errors. Cross-reference any new errors against the files in scope.

---

## Agent D — Test & story coverage

For each component file under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/`:
- A paired `*.stories.tsx` exists in the same directory (required by [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) > Testing).

**No — none of these are from our changes.** I checked our complete change set against every error's source file, and there's zero overlap. Here's each one:

| Error | Where it comes from | Ours? |
|---|---|---|
| `GithubLogo` / `FigmaLogo` not found in icons | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/home/**data.js**` — the **base template's demo home page** imports two icons the Zimmermann icon set doesn't include | ❌ No — base template, `node_modules`, home page. We didn't touch icons or home. |
| `experiences-components-react` "Failed to parse source map … .tsx … ENOENT" (×24) | `node_modules/@contentful/experiences-components-react` — a **third-party package** whose published `dist` points at `src/*.tsx` files it doesn't ship | ❌ No — benign dev-only source-map noise from a dependency. It's pulled in by the Contentful **Experiences** feature, which the PR already used *before* our fixes; our changes don't add or alter that dependency. |
| `useContentful.ts:116 … InvalidQuery … unknownContentType "DOESNOTEXIST"` + `400` | `overrides/app/hooks/**useContentful.ts**` — the **pre-existing REST hook** (`useContentfulEntries`), which we did **not** touch | ❌ No — different file. Our new hook is `useContentfulClient.ts`. Something else in the app is querying a content type literally named `DOESNOTEXIST` (a leftover/placeholder). |
| `Missing translation "header.button.assistive_msg.search"` | i18n / `translations/` | ❌ No — we didn't touch translations. |
| `useEinstein … Failed to fetch` | Einstein personalization API (unreachable in local dev) | ❌ No — environmental; Einstein isn't configured/reachable on localhost. |

**Evidence:** our change set is exactly `experience`, `contentfulPreview`, `useContentfulClient(.ts/.test.ts)`, `config/contentful.ts`, the doc, and the registry — and `git status` confirms **none** of `useContentful.ts`, `icons`, `pages/home`, `translations`, or `einstein` are in it.

**The positive signal:** not one of these messages references our files (`useContentfulClient`, `experience/index`, `contentfulPreview/index`) — so our code compiled and the app boots without our code throwing anything. That's real, but note it's still **not** a test of the must-fix — nothing here exercised `/preview` or `?preview`.

Two of these are pre-existing issues you *may* want tracked separately (not ours, not this PR): the **base home-page icon mismatch** (`GithubLogo`/`FigmaLogo`) and the **`DOESNOTEXIST` content-type query** in the old `useContentful.ts` — that one looks like a real leftover bug somewhere in the app.

Since the app's up: want me to help you actually exercise our must-fix now? Navigate to a real slug with `?preview` and to `/preview` — I can tell you exactly what to check (the `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` tag, and the 404 path if you point it at a no-token setup). That would finally give us the runtime confirmation we flagged as missing.

content.text:
Got the decisive facts. Two things shape the answer:

1. **Default site is `ZimmermannAU` at root** (`showDefaults: false`, no alias) — so test URLs need **no `/site/locale/` prefix**, just `localhost:3000/<slug>`.
2. **Your local `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` IS set** (in both `.env` and `.env.dev`) — this is the catch: with a token present, `?preview` will render **preview mode**, *not* our 404 gate. The must-fix 404 only fires when there's **no** token (i.e., prod).

So there are two different things to test:

## A) `?preview` path as-is (token present) — proves it renders + noindex, not the 404
```
http://localhost:3000/test-preview?preview
```
- Routes to `/:slug` → `Experience`, `isPreview=true`, token present → tries to fetch a `collectionPageExp` named `test-preview`.
- `test-preview` isn't real, so you'll see **"Page not found."** — but rendered **with `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">`** (verify in View Source). That confirms the preview render path + noindex wiring works and doesn't crash.
- For a *successful* render you need a **real** `collectionPageExp` slug — that's Contentful data, not in the code. I can query your Contentful space for a real one if you want (see below).

## B) The actual must-fix (the 404 gate) — the whole point of the fix
This only triggers with **no** preview token, so simulate prod:
1. Comment out `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` in `.env`, then `! npm start` to restart.
2. Hit:
   ```
   http://localhost:3000/test-preview?preview     → 404 + "Preview is not enabled in this environment." + noindex
   http://localhost:3000/preview                   → 404 + "Not found." + noindex
   ```
3. **This is exactly the bug we fixed:** before our change, `/test-preview?preview` returned **200 with no noindex** (indexable draft-preview on prod). Now it's 404 + noindex, matching `/preview`.
4. Restore the token afterward.

**What to verify (DevTools):**
- **Network tab** → the *document* request status: `404` on the gate paths.
- **Elements/View Source** → `<head>` contains `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">`.

## The slug you asked for
Use **`test-preview`** (any string works — the 404 gate short-circuits before any Contentful fetch, so it doesn't need to be real).

**I can't hand you a *real* Experience slug** — those live in your Contentful space, not the code (the content type is `collectionPageExp`). If you want a real one that actually renders, say the word and I'll query the Contentful Delivery API with your local token to list live `collectionPageExp` slugs/entry-IDs, then give you a URL that renders a real preview for case A.

2. **Merge `origin/develop`** into the branch (clean, +14 — must happen *after* the commit, since merge needs a clean tree).

## Proposed commit messages (conventional-commit, enforced by the hook)
Split into **code** + **docs** (cleanly separable; the reformat-vs-logic split I mentioned earlier isn't practical — it's entangled in the same files):

fix(contentful): gate ?preview no-token path with 404 + noindex (SFCC-49)

```

**1. The CodeRabbit local review.** AGENTS.md wants `cr review --light --base develop` *before* committing — but the CLI isn't installed here. Options:
- **(A)** You install it (`! npm i -g @coderabbitai/cli` per their docs, then `npm run env -- init`), I run the local review first.
- **(B)** Skip local; let the **PR-level CodeRabbit** (auto-runs on push) be the review gate. You've already manually verified the behaviour, so this is defensible — just not strictly per the doc.

**2. Commit shape:** the two-commit code/docs split above (my recommendation), or a single combined commit?

## Heads-up for merge (not blocking the push)
- **You're now the author**, and the commit touches **`config/contentful.ts` (Tier 1)** + the PR already includes **`routes.tsx` (Tier 2)**. Branch protection needs a **non-author** review — so **TimLavelleACC or mani** (a different tier-1-approver) must approve, not you.

Root cause pinned down — and it's a **config bug in the BrowserStack setup, not our code**:

**The problem:** The workflow runs `npx browserstack-node-sdk playwright test …` (qa.yml:456/459). That settles it. Here's the complete picture:

## The problem (precise root cause)
A **filename mismatch in the BrowserStack setup** — not a test failure, and not our code:
- The workflow runs `npx browserstack-node-sdk playwright test …` (qa.yml:456/459).
- `browserstack-node-sdk` looks for a config named **`browserstack.yml`** (no dot) by default.
- The repo's file is **`.browserstack.yml`** (with a dot), and the invocation never points the SDK at it (no `--config-file`, no `BROWSERSTACK_CONFIG_FILE`).
- → SDK finds no config, throws `Config file does not exist`, and dies **at setup, before running any test**.

## It's not ours, and it's pre-existing
- **Identical error** to the run before our changes (same `BrowserStackSetup.js` stack).
- `git log` on `.browserstack.yml` shows **one commit ever** ("Initial commit") — never touched by us or recently. Our diff is Contentful pages/hook/config/docs — zero BrowserStack surface.
- This job has effectively been broken since it was set up — a latent config bug.

## It does NOT block the merge ✅
I checked develop's branch protection — the **required** checks are only:
- **Storybook interaction & a11y** ✅ green
- **Unit tests (Vitest)** ✅ green
- **🔴 Branch Target Check** ✅ green

**"Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)" is *not* a required check** — it's advisory. So this red mark won't stop the merge. The PR's `BLOCKED` state is due to the **review requirement** (CODEOWNERS wants a tier-1 approving review for `config/contentful.ts` — i.e., Tim), *not* this failure.

## The fix — Integration's, not this PR's
`.browserstack.yml` and `.github/workflows/qa.yml` are both **Tier 1 (Integration/SI Partner)**, so I won't touch them here (out of scope, and it'd cross tiers). For Integration, it's a one-liner either way:
- point the SDK at the file — `npx browserstack-node-sdk --config-file .browserstack.yml …` (or set `BROWSERSTACK_CONFIG_FILE`) in qa.yml **and** `scripts/runStoryTests.sh`, **or**
- rename `.browserstack.yml` → `browserstack.yml`.

**Bottom line:** the only red on the PR is a pre-existing BrowserStack config bug that (a) isn't ours and (b) doesn't block the merge. All three required checks are green; PR #43 is now gated only on Tim's review. Fetched. The **07:51 review added 3 findings** on top of the 07:44 two. Here's my review of the complete open set — I verified each rather than reflexively agreeing:

## The 3 new findings (07:51)

**Finding 3 — 🟡 `02-contentful.md:73`: duplicated "only"** — ✅ valid, trivial
The §3 "Live preview" bullet reads *"only set on dev/test/sit/uat only"*. Redundant. **Pre-existing prose** (not text we wrote — our doc edits were the diagram/§4/§9), but it's a one-word fix in a file we're already in. → **Fix.**

**Finding 4 — 🟠 `experience:48`: not-found path returns soft-200** — ⚠️ valid concern, but scope + a real subtlety
The `error || !experience` branch renders "Page not found." at HTTP 200. A genuine missing slug *should* 404 (soft-404s are bad SEO) — CodeRabbit's right in spirit. **But two problems with applying it here:**
- It's **pre-existing** and **outside your 5-request scope** — and it's on the **public `/:slug` delivery route** (not the preview-only path), so it changes public HTTP semantics — higher blast radius.
- **CodeRabbit's exact fix is subtly wrong:** it says 404 on `error || !experience`, but `error` can be a *transient Contentful API failure*, not a genuine not-found. Returning **404 on a fetch error is incorrect** (should be a 5xx/retry, not "gone"). A correct fix must distinguish `error` from `!experience`. → **Recommend deferring** (or doing carefully, if you want it in).

**Finding 5 — 🟡 `experience:114`: `!client` config-missing state is indexable 200** — ⚠️ valid-ish, pre-existing edge case
If Contentful config is missing in prod, the `!client` branch shows an internal error at 200. Real but **extreme edge case** (prod config broken = whole-site Contentful outage), **pre-existing**, out of scope. → **Recommend deferring** (bundle with #4 if you choose to harden the experience page).

## Recap of the 07:44 two
- **Finding 2 — 🟠 `contentfulPreview:157` `!entryId` missing noindex** — ✅ **valid, fix.** Editor-only `/preview` route should be uniformly noindex; this completes that invariant (low blast radius, in-theme).
- **Finding 1 — 🟡 `components.md:59` "Register must be 7"** — ❌ **false positive.** Verified: re-running the generator yields `Register`=3 with zero diff — it's generator output, not a hand-edit. Reply, don't fix.

| Finding | Verdict | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 2 — `!entryId` noindex | ✅ valid, in-scope | **Fix** |
| 3 — doc "only only" | ✅ valid, trivial | **Fix** |
| 1 — Register count | ❌ false positive | **Reply, don't fix** |
| 4 — not-found 404 | ⚠️ valid, out-of-scope + nuanced | **Defer** (separate ticket) — or fix carefully if you want it in |
| 5 — `!client` 404/noindex | ⚠️ valid, out-of-scope edge case | **Defer** — or bundle with #4 |

The clean, in-scope path: **fix 2 + 3, reply-reject 1, and reply-defer 4 + 5** (with a note that they're pre-existing public-route hardening for a follow-up — and that #4 needs error-vs-not-found care). That keeps this PR true to your 5 without silently absorbing pre-existing bugs.

content.text:
I have to correct myself: **it's not a false positive. I was wrong earlier, and here's exactly why.**

My earlier "verification" (re-run generator → `Register`=3, no diff) was misleading me — that regen was a **cache hit serving stale data**, not a fresh computation. The evidence now:

- The generator caches base-component counts in **`.baseCache.json`** — **gitignored/local-only**, keyed by base-package version (`10.0.0`), built **July 9**.
- That version hasn't changed, so every regen re-emits the **cached `3`** — regardless of the actual code.
- A **fresh** `countConsumers('register')` returns **7**. That's what CodeRabbit computed, and it's what a cache-miss (e.g. CI on a clean checkout) would produce.

So CodeRabbit correctly caught that the committed `3` is **stale**. Good thing you had me double-check.

## But two important nuances
1. **The metric is a crude substring grep**, not a real import graph. The `countConsumers` logic is `grep -rl "register"`. The 7 "matches" are mostly this:
   ```
   // Side-effect import — registers experience components with the Contentful Experiences SDK
   ```
   i.e. **"registers experience components"** — Contentful *Experiences* registration, which has **nothing to do with the base `Register` (account signup) component.** So `7` isn't meaningfully "correct" either — both `3` and `7` are noise.
2. **It's 100% pre-existing and not from our PR.** The cache predates the whole Contentful preview feature (July 9), those `registers` comments are mani's, and our regen just faithfully served the local cache as designed. (And CI passed with `3` committed — there's no registry-freshness gate, so it doesn't block anything.)

## So it's a real-but-stale generated value in a noisy metric. Options:
- **A) Bust `.baseCache.json` + regenerate** → registry shows fresh counts (`Register` 3→7, **plus every other base row that drifted since July 9** — likely broad, unrelated churn). Closes the finding but adds noise.
- **B) Leave it + reply** explaining the stale-cache mechanism, and flag the generator's cache-invalidation as a **separate tooling ticket** (the real fix). Keeps this PR scoped. ← **my recommendation**
- **C)** Bust + regenerate as an isolated `chore(registry)` commit (delineated from the feature).

## Recommended reply (Option B) — honest, not a "false positive" dismissal:
> Fair catch that `3` ≠ a fresh count. It's not a hand-edit though: the `Consumers` column is generated by `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs`, which caches base-component counts in a gitignored, local-only `.baseCache.json` keyed by base-package version (`@salesforce/retail-react-app@10.0.0`). That version hasn't changed since the cache was built (Jul 9), so every regen re-emits the cached `3`, while a fresh `countConsumers` grep now returns `7`.
>
> Two caveats: (1) this is a crude substring count — the extra matches are `// …registers experience components` comments (Contentful Experiences registration), unrelated to the base `Register` account component, so neither `3` nor `7` is a meaningful consumer count; (2) it's pre-existing and unrelated to this PR. The proper fix is the generator's cache invalidation (refresh on overrides drift, not just base-version bumps) — raising that separately rather than hand-editing a generated file or busting the cache here (which sweeps in unrelated base-count churn).

Which option do you want — **B** (reply + separate ticket, my rec), **A/C** (refresh the counts now), or something else? Once you pick, I'll post the reply (and open the tooling ticket if you want).

content.text:
Verified the mechanics — and this changes #4. Here's the evidence:

`useFetchByBase` (what `useFetchBySlug` uses):
```js
"use client";
const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(isSupervisedMode(mode) ? false : true); // starts TRUE
useEffect(() => { /* the actual fetch */ }, [fetchMethod, mode]);  // runs client-side only
```
Plus `Experience` has **no `getProps`** (only `getTemplateName`) — so there's **no SSR prefetch**. That means:

## #4 is NOT a quick win — CodeRabbit's fix would be dead code
- During **SSR**, `isLoading` starts `true` → the component renders the **Spinner at HTTP 200**. The `error || !experience` branch is **never reached server-side**.
- The not-found state is only known **after the client-side `useEffect` fetch resolves** — by which point `res` (from `useServerContext`) is **`undefined`** (it only exists during SSR).
- So `res.status(404)` in that branch **can never run where `res` exists** → it sets nothing. A real 404 for a missing slug would require adding **SSR data-fetching (`getProps`) to the experience page** — a much bigger, out-of-scope change to the public route's data flow.
- Achievable now: only `<Seo noIndex/>` (client-rendered, so JS-crawlers like Google respect it — but the page still SSRs a 200 Spinner).

## #5 IS fixable — but the status should be 500, not 404
`!client` is **synchronous** (config read, no async), so it *is* reached during SSR with `res` available → a status *can* be set. But "Contentful configuration is missing" is a **server misconfiguration → 500**, not a 404 (a 404 would falsely tell crawlers the URL doesn't exist). So: `<Seo noIndex/>` + `res.status(500)`.

## So "both quick wins" holds for #5, not #4. Recommendation:
- **#5:** fix now — `<Seo noIndex/>` + `res.status(500)`. ✅ clean.
- **#4:** add `<Seo noIndex/>` now (honest partial — stops JS-crawlers indexing the soft-404), and **reply + follow-up ticket** for the real 404 (needs SSR prefetch). I won't ship the dead-code `res.status(404)`.

This is me not blindly applying a review suggestion that doesn't actually work in this architecture. Two quick decisions:
1. **#5 status: 500** (my rec, semantically correct) or CodeRabbit's **404**?
2. **#4: noindex-only + follow-up ticket** (my rec), or **defer #4 entirely**, or **do the full `getProps` SSR-prefetch** now (bigger, I'd advise against in this PR)?

`mergeState: BLOCKED` — waiting on **Tim's tier-1 approving review** (the CODEOWNERS gate for `config/contentful.ts`). That's the real and only substantive blocker now.
